REPO: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, HEAD `ac224a6`.

Fetch full text: `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/comments/<ID> --jq '.body'`

YOUR FIVE:
- **B1** `3841133771` — `components/footer/index.tsx:180` — "Clear stale footer data before a replacement request."
- **B2** `3841133778` — `components/footer/index.tsx:183` — "Name the Contentful request contract values."
- **B3** `3841133783` (**Major**) — `components/header/index.tsx:372` — "Add the Account control to the mobile header."
- **B4** `3841133792` — `ui-kits/atoms/zimmLogo/index.stories.tsx:70` — "Name the logo sample widths."
- **B5** `3841133810` (**Major**) — `ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/zimmModal.css.ts:30` — "Make oversized modal content scrollable."

CONSTRAINTS:
- **READ-ONLY.** No edits/staging/commits/stashes/checkouts — other agent sessions are writing to this tree. Test variants only in `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/`.
- You MAY run `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, `npm run build-storybook`.

CRITICAL CONTEXT:

**B3 is a product/scope question, not a code one, and needs careful handling.** This PR is SFCC-55, scoped to the *global footer*. `header/index.tsx` is Tier 2 shared shell (`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, Global Shell, owner: both squads). Determine: (a) does the mobile header genuinely lack an Account control? (b) is there a requirement for it — search `.docs/prd/` for HPC-018 or any header requirement naming Search/Account/Bag; (c) does `header/index.tsx` contain commented-out base SFCC account/wishlist icon buttons with a comment explaining why they're disabled? (d) what did this branch actually change in that file — `git diff ec9d161..HEAD -- overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`. AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 says never refactor upward: fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours. Judge whether this belongs in SFCC-55 at all.

**B5 may be a genuine a11y defect.** WCAG 2.2 AA is the project target (AGENTS.md). Read `zimmModal.css.ts`'s `panel` part and determine whether tall content can overflow without being reachable — check for `maxHeight`, `overflow`, `overflowY`. Then check what actually renders inside it: `ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx`. Is the content short enough that overflow is unreachable in practice, or could it clip on a small viewport? WCAG 1.4.10 (reflow) and 2.1.1 (keyboard) are the relevant criteria. Note the modal ships behind `enableNameCapture`, which defaults to `false` — check that and factor reachability into severity.

**B1** — read the `useEffect` in `footer/index.tsx` around `:170-205`. Determine whether a site change triggers a refetch while stale data from the previous site remains rendered. Check the dependency array and whether `setFooterData(null)` is called before the new request. Consider: this is a multi-site storefront (8 storefronts), so a site switch mid-session is the scenario. Does the app actually remount on site change, making this unreachable? Check `useMultiSite` and the routing setup before concluding.

**B2 and B4** — judge against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`'s "No magic numbers or strings" rule, and against what the repo actually does. For B2, check whether `include: 3` and the content type string appear elsewhere and whether a constants module already exists (look at `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`). For B4, check whether the literals are in a `.stories.tsx` file — note `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` explicitly excludes `*.stories.tsx` from its raw-value scan, which suggests a deliberate policy about story files. Quote the exclusion if so.

REPORT per finding: **CLAIM TRUE / FALSE / PARTLY**, then **FIX / DECLINE / DEFER**, exact change if FIX, quotable rule/measurement if DECLINE, effort, and for B3/B5 an explicit in-scope-for-SFCC-55 judgement. Lead with B5 then B3. Be terse; quote line numbers.

Investigation complete. All five verified from source; B5 measured empirically in a headless browser.

## B5 — `zimmModal.css.ts:30` "Make oversized modal content scrollable" (Major)

**CLAIM TRUE → FIX.**

Structurally confirmed: overlay is `position:fixed; inset:0` + `align-items:center` with `overflow` unset (`zimmModal.css.ts:9-22`); `panel` (`:26-30`) has no `maxHeight`/`overflow`. There is **no** scroll path in any direction — the overlay is `fixed` (body scroll can't move it) *and* `useZimmModal.ts:69` sets `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'`. Centre-alignment splits the overflow, so roughly half is clipped **above** the viewport top and is unreachable by scroll, Tab-scroll, or `scrollIntoView`.

Measured (replicated resolved styles — 480px `MODAL_MAX_WIDTH`, 40px panel padding, 45px field rows, 41px `BTN_HEIGHT_SM`; probe at `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/b5probe/`):

| viewport | panel H | clipped above | clipped below | title reachable | Continue reachable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320×256 (**WCAG 1.4.10** reflow target) | 533 | **138** | 139 | ✗ | ✗ |
| 667×375 (SE landscape, real device, no zoom) | 461 | **43** | 43 | ✗ | ✗ |
| 640×400 (1280×800 @200% zoom, **WCAG 1.4.4**) | 461 | **30** | 31 | ✓ | ✓ |
| 375×667 (SE portrait) | 497 | 0 | 0 | ✓ | ✓ |

Even a font-metric-independent floor (padding 80 + title 18+40 + fields 45+24+45+40 + two single-line paragraphs 18+16+18+40 + actions 41 = **425px**) exceeds the 216px available at the 1.4.10 target, so the failure doesn't depend on font fallback or wrap estimates.

**Exact change** (2 lines, `zimmModal.css.ts` panel part):
```ts
maxHeight: '100%',
overflowY: 'auto',
```
Prefer `maxHeight: '100%'` over CodeRabbit's `calc(100dvh - var(--zimm-scale-l) - var(--zimm-scale-l))`. Both measured **identically clean** at all four viewports, but the `calc` restates the overlay's own `padding` in a second place — the drift risk `overrideStyling.md` ("The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy") warns about. `100%` resolves against the overlay's border-box content box (Chakra's CSS reset sets `box-sizing: border-box`), so it self-maintains if the overlay padding ever changes. Neither trips `audit:tokens` (`UNIT_RE` is `rem|em|px` only).

**In scope for SFCC-55: yes.** `zimmModal.css.ts` is a file this PR *creates* (`git diff --name-status` → `A`), it's the co-located recipe of an atom this PR introduces, and CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule routes it to the owning squad — no Tier 1/2 designer gate. Not refactoring upward.

**Severity caveat, worth stating in the reply:** unreachable by shoppers *today*. `enableNameCapture` defaults `false` (`footer/index.tsx:62`, `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:45`), gating the modal at `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:82`; nothing outside stories sets it. But the defect lives in the **shared** atom whose docblock says "any future dialog… can reuse the same accessible shell" — so every future modal inherits it, and axe can't detect clipping. Fix now at 2 lines. Effort: **~5 min** (+~10 if you also add a `TallContent` story to `zimmModal/index.stories.tsx`, which currently only renders a 2-element dialog).

## B3 — `header/index.tsx:372` "Add the Account control to the mobile header" (Major)

**CLAIM PARTLY TRUE → DECLINE the code change; FIX one inaccurate comment this PR added.**

(a) **TRUE.** The mobile cluster (`:358`, `display={{base:'flex', lg:'none'}}`) renders Search, Store Locator, Bag — no Account. The `Account` text button (`:238-246`) sits inside `display={{base:'none', lg:'flex'}}`, so it is desktop-only.

(b) **TRUE and quotable.** `.docs/prd/homepage.md:18-19`: "The confirmed header icon set is: **Search, Account, and Bag** (HPC-018). Locate Boutique, Contact Us, and Newsletter are **not part of the header** — confirmed per design review on 23 June 2026." Store Locator does render on mobile (`config/default.js:36 storeLocatorEnabled: true`), so it does contradict HPC-018.

(c) **TRUE.** Commented-out base `IconButtonWithRegistration` Account + Wishlist block at `:373-394`, with the explanatory comment at `:368-372`.

(d) **What this PR actually changed there: comments only.** `git diff cd68e97..HEAD -- overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx` = **+14 / -0**, all comment lines (commit `77042f8 docs(header): explain the disabled base SFCC icon-button block`). The only other header touch is a one-word comment path fix in `theme/components/header.ts` (`button.ts` → `zimmButton.css.ts`). Zero functional or visual header changes in this PR.

**Also: mobile Account access is not actually absent.** There is no `drawer-menu` override, so the base `drawer-menu.jsx` ships — it has "My Account" (`:235-236`) and "Sign in" (`:287`), opened by the mobile-only hamburger at `:196-212`. HPC-025 (`homepage.md:23`) confirms mobile chrome deliberately differs by surfacing controls in the burger menu. So this is a **design-parity question, not a functional dead end**, and CodeRabbit produced no Figma reference for the mobile header icon set.

**Decline rationale to quote:** `header/index.tsx` is Tier 2 Global Shell, "Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching" (`protectedFiles.md`). SFCC-55 is the global *footer*; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 ("Never refactor upward") and #10 (one protection tier per change) both bite. Adding an Account icon and removing Store Locator from mobile would be this PR's first functional touch of the shared header, with no mobile-header Figma spec and no ticket.

**But do fix this, because the PR introduced it:** the comment added at `:370` (and the twin at the icons import) asserts *"HPC-018 requires Search / Account / Bag in the header; Account ships as text, so nothing is missing."* That is true at `lg`+ and **false below `lg`**. Reword to scope the claim to desktop, note mobile Account lives in the burger drawer, and note the Store Locator icon on mobile is an open HPC-018 discrepancy for a follow-up ticket. Effort: **~5 min** (2 comment blocks) + raise the follow-up.

## B1 — `footer/index.tsx:180` "Clear stale footer data before a replacement request"

**CLAIM FALSE (unreachable) → DECLINE.**

The state transition the finding depends on cannot occur. `site` comes from `MultiSiteContext`, fed by `MultiSiteProvider site={locals.site}` (`_app-config/index.tsx:155`). `locals.site` is only ever set by `AppConfig.restore` (`:171-210`), and `restore` is called in exactly two places in the SDK — `ssr/server/react-rendering.js:136` (per request) and `ssr/browser/main.js:107` (once at hydration). **It is never re-run on a client-side route change**, so `site.id` is fixed for the lifetime of a mounted `FooterContainer`. Consistently, every site/locale switch is a full document load — even the base footer's own selector does `window.location = ...` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/footer/index.jsx:156`) — which remounts the whole tree.

The `client` half is also a non-scenario: `useContentfulClient.ts:44-47` memoises on `[spaceId, environment, token, host]`, all static env config, so it never goes truthy → falsy mid-session.

The proposed `setFooterData(null)` would be **inert**, not wrong: on the only run that ever happens, `footerData` is already `null`. Declining avoids code defending an architecturally impossible state. `site.id` in the dep array is correct as defensive hygiene. Existing coverage (`index.test.tsx:145` "renders nothing while the fetch is pending") already proves the documented loading behaviour for the reachable path. Effort if overruled: **~2 min**, zero risk.

## B2 — `footer/index.tsx:183` "Name the Contentful request contract values"

**CLAIM PARTLY TRUE → FIX (cheaper and better than proposed).**

The string half is stronger than CodeRabbit realised: a constant **already exists** — `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53-59` exports `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` including `footerConfig: 'footerConfig'` (landed on this branch at `5b2be3f`). `footer/index.tsx:183` is the only place bypassing it. No new constant needed:

```ts
import { CONTENT_TYPE_IDS } from 'app/config/contentfulMapping';
// Contentful resolves nested references `include` levels deep:
// footerConfig → navGroups (1) → links (2) → region (3).
const FOOTER_INCLUDE_DEPTH = 3;
...
.getEntries({ content_type: CONTENT_TYPE_IDS.footerConfig, include: FOOTER_INCLUDE_DEPTH })
```

`include: 3` is a genuine magic number under `conventions.md` ("No magic numbers or strings… Excepted: `0`, `1`, `-1`"), and naming it is worth more than usual here because `useContentful.ts:110` hardcodes a *different* depth (`include=2`) — a reader currently can't tell why footer needs 3. Effort: **~5 min**, tsc-neutral (baseline `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean).

Optional consistency follow-up, same PR, 1 line: `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19` passes the raw `'uiCopy'` where `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS.uiCopy` exists.

## B4 — `zimmLogo/index.stories.tsx:70` "Name the logo sample widths"

**CLAIM FALSE → DECLINE.** Quotable, from `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:11-17`:

> Deliberately excludes: … `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx` — test assertions and Storybook demo code routinely need **illustrative/representative raw values** that aren't "a hardcoded design value shipped to production" in the sense this audit cares about (testing.md already treats these differently from production styling rigor).

`[160, 240, 320]` is exactly that: three arbitrary demo widths whose only purpose is to be rendered as the visible label `{w}px` (`:73`) — they *are* the story's subject, covered by `conventions.md`'s own carve-out for "string literals that _are_ the value (e.g. CSS class names, JSX text)". Naming them `LOGO_SAMPLE_WIDTHS` adds indirection and zero information; there is no second call site to keep in sync.

Corroborating: a confirmed run of `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` lists 16 acknowledged + 14 unacknowledged findings and **not one story file among them** — the same file already uses bare theme keys (`bg="background.05"`, `mb={2}`) that `overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 forbids in component files, precisely because stories play by looser rules. Effort: reply only.

---

Summary: **1 fix (B5, a real WCAG 1.4.10/1.4.4 defect), 1 partial fix (B2), 1 scope decline + comment correction (B3), 2 declines (B1 false, B4 false).** No files were modified; the only writes were the probe under `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/b5probe/`.
